newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS LOWERS CERTAIN PLACER DOME DEBT.
newsitem.headline: CBRS LOWERS CERTAIN PLACER DOME DEBT.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Tuesday that it lowered its ratings on the senior unsecured and junior subordinated long-term debt of Placer Dome Inc.

CBRS said it rated Place Dome's US$600 million of senior unsecured debt securities at A(Low), down from single A. It also rated the company's US$300 million of junior subordinated debt at B++(Low), down from B++.
The rating on Placer Dome's US$300 million commercial paper remained unchanged at A-1/Prime Quality, CBRS said. The revised ratings have a stable outlook, it said.
The revisions came after the rating agency's annual credit assessment of Placer Dome, CBRS said.

While continuing to signify the good quality credit standing for Placer Dome's long-term debt securities, the revised ratings reflect the weaker-than-expected financial performance of the company over the past two and a half years, a period during which gold prices declined significantly, CBRS said.
That reduced the earnings protection and overall credit quality of the company, CBRS said.

The agency said the company's cashflow generation will likely fall short of its capital spending estimates in 1997 to 1999 in light of its objective to maintain aggressive growth through new mine development projects.
Increased production from the Pipeline and Musselwhite projects, however, will significantly increase gold production, while lowering the average cost of production at Placer Dome, CBRS said.
